cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Efficiency Win
cards.instruction: Celebrate each inconvenience as proof that a faster, cheaper, or smarter routine can now be invented.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The dishwasher's broken. Excellent, I'll run a plate-free dinner: curry in rolls, no washing-up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Twelve guests, six rolls. How are you serving everyone?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Halves. Twice the servings, same bread. You choose the cuts; I'll fit the curry around them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll cut them, but that curry will run straight off a flat half.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll hollow each half. You decide how much bread to leave; I'll stir the crumbs into the curry. Thicker filling, edible bowls, and we've saved the flour. Good team.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 leads a plate-free service; A3 gives cutting control and A5 bowl depth to B while repeatedly celebrating problems as resource savings.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 count problem causes A3 halves; B4 runoff problem causes A5 hollowing and using removed bread as thickener.

relationship.evidence: B2 asks a real service question and B4 agrees to help with a practical caveat; A incorporates that expertise.

heightening.evidence: A5 turns the caveat into both edible bowls and saved thickener, preserving the efficiency game.

specificity.evidence: A1 curry/dishwasher and B2 twelve-to-six arithmetic make the improvised routine specific.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 good team is a modest confidence-preserving tag after actual cooperative concessions.
